outcome: Percentage of ossification area (front and hind extremities)
cohort: Thirty pregnant female Wistar albino rats were used, and their fetuses were examined for developmental outcomes.
finding: Nonylphenol exposure negatively impacted fetal and placenta weights, body and head lengths, and bone development (length and ossification area), while curcumin treatments showed protective effects similar to the control group by accelerating bone formation.
cross-section timing: N/A (observations were made on the 20th day of pregnancy in rats)
birth_weight: Fetus weights were measured on day 20 of gestation (lowest in the nonylphenol group offspring).
gest_age: Observations were made at 20 days of gestation.
